svg.text: CONCEPT — the assembly as decided, nothing built yet
TWO STRUTS, TWO CLAMPS, TWO FEET, NO MAGNETS
Clamped to the side panel top and bottom, standing on the floor. The clamps grip; the floor carries; nothing magnetic is involved.

THE TWO PARTS
THE BASE — 3.1x, in elevation
at side-elevation scale this whole arrangement is 3 px
floor

underside 15
MEASURED 10-20
clamp long leg — UNDER the cabinet
clamp short leg
rises OUTSIDE
foot
floor pad 3
A — spanning clamp bar x2
One bar per surface, reaching across BOTH struts — 301 mm
front-to-back. That is what ties the two struts into a frame;
widening the individual parts would only add steel that is not
joined to anything at its far end. Long leg on the fridge top,
or under its base. ELEVATOR BOLTS through square laser-cut
holes are the studs: a flat 2.78 mm head that hides inside the
foam, and a square shoulder that stops it spinning. No
welding. The lower one is the same part, flipped, bearing on
two pads because the underside is not flat.
B — slotted foot x2
L bracket. Vertical leg carries the elongated slot the stud
passes through; horizontal leg turns OUTBOARD and the strut
stands on it, so the strut never touches the floor. The
inboard foot was deleted as redundant.
THE BASE JOINT — 4.5x
section through one stud, looking along the fridge face
OPEN face — plate bolts here
fridge
foam 3
clamp 3.02
foot 3.02
strut WEB 1.78
nut INSIDE the channel
ELEVATOR bolt, 5/16-18 x 1 in
head 30.2 dia x 2.78 thick, FLAT — it hides inside
the 3 mm foam and never touches the panel. A carriage
bolt's dome would stand 2.08 mm proud of the same foam.
The slots are in the strut's BACK WEB, so the bolt only has
to reach 7.83 mm of material plus a nut — 3/4 in would do,
1 in is comfortable. The nut sits INSIDE the channel.
square neck 8.38 across x 4.83 long locks in the
CLAMP's square hole and passes 1.80 mm beyond, so the
FOOT slot must clear 8.38 mm, not just the shank.
THE STACK, PANEL TO SCREEN — true scale
fridge panel

STRUT 20.64

75.7 mm — and 66.7 of it cannot be designed away
Assembly
1. Stand the struts on the feet; stud through foot slot and strut slot, nut loose.
2. Hook the top clamps over the fridge top; washers behind the strut; nut loose.
3. Slide the lower clamps UP their slots until they engage under the appliance.
4. Lock everything. The struts go into tension and the fridge is gripped.
STILL OPEN — both need a torch under the fridge
- Does a 150-250 mm clamp reach foul anything under there? Compressor, tubing, insulation, cross-members. It sets how far the
lower clamp can go in, and nothing else can answer it.
- Is there a downward-facing rib or lip within reach? If so, HOOKING it beats bearing on it — a hook has no compliance at all,
where foam has a little.
- The gap under the side measured 10-20 mm and the underside is NOT flat, so the lower clamp's short leg plus its foam has to live
inside that, at its tightest.
